mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to expectations of tighter policy and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: In a rising FEDFUNDS regime, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in at least 70% of instances, or the 5-day realized return does not lag the 20-day forecast by more than 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 2-month decline in FEDFUNDS below the prior 6-month average predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate further easing and lower borrowing costs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < (6-month rolling avg FEDFUNDS) for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, the 60-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10) or the realized 60-day return is less than the predicted return by more than 1.5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market activity) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (unemployment) signals a strong labor market, which typically precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > (prev(PAYEMS) + 10%) AND UNRATE < (prev(UNRATE) - 0.5%) in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening with low unemployment
failure_condition: During periods matching the trigger, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 40% of cases, or the 5-day realized return does not exceed the 20-day forecast by at least 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (household spending) rises by at least 5% over the next quarter relative to the prior quarter, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as consumer confidence improves.
failure_condition: In 60-day windows after the trigger, the 60-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of instances, or the realized return is less than the forecast by more than 3 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 2% suggests weakening supply-side constraints, which tends to produce a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates slower growth.
failure_condition: During INDPRO contraction months, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in over 60% of cases, or the 5-day realized return exceeds the 20-day forecast by more than 1 percentage point.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 5.0% for three consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent high rates and reduced equity risk appetite.
failure_condition: In the 20-day window following the three-month high-rate regime, the forward return is positive in at least 60% of instances, or the realized return beats the forecast by more than 1.5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS accompanied by a sustained drop in UNRATE (over two consecutive months) indicates a tight labor market, which usually precedes a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > (prev(PAYEMS) * 1.12) AND UNRATE < (prev(UNRATE) - 0.8) for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During the two-month trigger, the 5-day forward return is negative in more than 80% of windows, or the realized 5-day return is less than the predicted return by more than 1 percentage point.

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip decline in RSAFS (retail sales) and INDPRO (industrial production) in the same month suggests deteriorating demand-supply conditions, which is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < (prev(RSAFS) * 0.95) AND INDPRO < (prev(INDPRO) * 0.97) in the same month
failure_condition: During months matching the trigger, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in over 50% of instances, or the realized return exceeds the forecast by more than 2 percentage points.
